description_en: Ikhālakhu Phalcā has recently been rebuilt using 'traditional' materials: wood and bricks. The iron railings have been removed. Attached to the southern wall of the Bāla Vidyāśrama primary school, it has three front bays and two side bays. Before 2021, the roof of the Phalcā was made ofjhĩgaṭītiles and all its bays are fenced with iron railings. The construction was of cement (e.g., plinth) and plain wodden pillars and beams.The local Śreṣṭha community (known as Sāhukhalaḥ, the trader clan) built this Phalcā. The traders used to buy copper sheets in India, use them to finish various pots in the Haugaḥ and Cakrabahila Ṭolas, and sell the final products in various parts of Nepal, sometimes even exporting the products to neighbouring countries. Among those traders, the Bhājukṛṣṇa Śreṣṭha were very popular. There is no historical evidence with which date the Phalcā. However, we known that this clan was counted amongst the wealthiest traders of the Kathmandu Valley in the Rāṇā period. It is therefore possible that the Phalcā was built at this time.The purpose of this Phalcā is very different from otherphalcās. When a member of the Sāhukhalaḥ dies, an idol of a deity is placed in this Phalcā in their memory. The statues are embedded in wall inches and cover all walls. A statue of Viṣṇu is placed to commemorate a man's death, whilst one of Lakṣmī is erected to commemorate a woman. Many of the installed statues have been taken, and an iron railing has been fixed around the bays to protect them. Currently, there are 20 statues of Viṣṇu and Lakṣmī in the Phalcā. A family member comes every morning to the Phalcā and offers water to the deities in the memory of their ancestors. Tradition also requests that the family of a newly married young man from the clan must arrange a wedding feast in this Phalcā.
description_ne: यो फल्चा इखालखुको बाल विद्याश्रम प्राथमिक विद्यालयको दक्षिणी गाह्रोसँग टाँस्सिएर रहेको छ । यो फल्चा इखालखुका 'साहुखलः' भनी चिनिने श्रेष्ठहरूले बनाएका हुन् । उनीहरू ललितपुरका धनी व्यापारी थिए । भारतबाट कच्चा तामा आयात गरेर इखालखुको नजीकै रहेको हौगः र चक्र बहिल टोलमा तामाका भाँडाकुँडा बनाई ती भाँडा नेपालका विभिन्न ठाउँमा अनि विदेशमा पनि निर्यात गर्ने गर्थे । ती व्यापारीमध्ये भाजुकृष्ण श्रेष्ठ निकै चर्चित थिए । यो फल्चा कहिले बनाइएको थियो भन्ने कुरा स्पष्ट पार्ने ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण प्राप्त छैन । राणाकालमा तिनीहरूको व्यापार निकै चम्केको थियो । सम्भवतः राणाकालमै यो फल्चा बनाइएको हुनुपर्छ ।अन्य फल्चाभन्दा यो फल्चाको प्रयोजन निकै भिन्न रहेको छ । यो फल्चामा साहुखलःको परिवारको कुनै सदस्यको मृत्यु भएमा उसको नाममा मूर्ति बनाएर स्थापना गरिन्छ । पुरुषको मृत्यु भएमा विष्णुको र महिलाको मृत्यु भएमा लक्ष्मीको मूर्ति बनाएर स्थापना गरिन्छ । यहाँ स्थापना गरिएका धेरै मूर्तिहरू हराइसके । चोरी हुनबाट रोक्न फल्चामा अहिले फलामको रेलिङ्ग लगाइएको छ । अहिले यहाँ विष्णु, लक्ष्मी र विष्णु-लक्ष्मीको गरी जम्मा २० वटा मूर्तिहरू रहेका छन् । मृत्यु भएका व्यक्तिको नाममा फल्चामा मूर्ति स्थापन गर्ने परिवारको सदस्यले प्रत्येक दिन बिहान सबेरै आफूले स्थापना गरेको मूर्ति पूजा गरी जल चढाउने परम्परा छ । इखालखुका साहुखलःको कुनै युवकको बिहे भएपछि परिवारका सदस्यहरू एवं इष्टमित्रहरू यस फल्चामा बसेर बिहेको भोज खाने परम्परा छ ।
monument_assessment: Slightly damaged (minor damages such as minor cracks, plants, missing stones in plinths)

historical_events.event_description: Vīṇā, Vinoda and Suvīna installed a Viṣṇu statue (LAL4245-011) in memory of the late Sūryakṛṣṇa Śreṣṭha.
Vinoda Kṛṣṇa Śreṣṭha and his wife installed a statue of Viṣṇu-Lakṣmī (LAL4245-014) in memory of their late nephew Savina Kṛṣṇa Śreṣṭha and his wife.
A statue of Viṣṇu-Lakṣmī (LAL4245-015) was installed in memory of Nārāyaṇakṛṣṇa Śreṣṭha (VS 1978-2071) and Kadamalatā Śreṣṭha (VS 1982-2071).
Sūryakṛṣṇa Śreṣṭha and Vinodakṛṣṇa Śreṣṭha installed a statue of Viṣṇu-Lakṣmī in memory of their late father Candrakṛṣṇa Śreṣṭha and mother Kuntīdevī Śreṣṭha.
A Viṣṇu statue was installed in memory of Rojakṛṣṇa Śreṣṭha (VS 2009-2075).
A Viṣṇu statue (LAL4245-020) was installed in memory of Cainakṛṣṇa.

Between 2019 and 2021, Ikhālakhu Phalcā, then built in cement, has been rebuilt using wood and brick, no historic materials have been used. The niches with deities have been removed, in March 2022, the statues made from stone have been placed on wooden shelves.
